museumIntro: Tilt your fixed cannon with Left/Right or A/D and press Space to fire at the falling robots. Intercept all eight to finish. Aim ahead of a robot so your shot meets it; slower falling robots give you more time. Hit a parachute to make its robot fall faster; it counts as intercepted when it hits the ground. A direct robot hit intercepts it immediately.

museumStory.title: Early 1980s: defending one patch of sky
museumStory.text:
Games of this type appeared on early home computers. Sabotage, made by Mark Allen for the Apple II in 1981, was followed by Greg Kuperberg’s Paratrooper for the IBM PC in 1982. The player aimed from a fixed position while aircraft and parachutes crossed the screen.

Sky Patrol adapts that setup with parachuting robots. It gives you a compact way to explore aiming, the path of a shot and what happens when two moving objects meet.
museumStory.prompt: What if your cannon tilted faster? Would it be easier to aim at a robot on the other side?
